newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS - FUEL OIL UP, BACKWARDATED.
newsitem.headline: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS - FUEL OIL UP, BACKWARDATED.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps extended its week long rally at midday on Thursday as the market flipped into backwardation on strong prompt physical buying interest, traders said.
"Fuel oil is very strong right now because of the physical buying and prompt supplies are tight," one trader said.
September fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $105.00/$105.50 per tonne, up from Wednesday's $104.00/$105.00, brokers said. It traded in the morning at $105.00 and $105.25, they said.
October on the other hand was last quoted at $104.75/$105.50 from Wednesday's $104.50/$105.50 in quiet trade.
As a result, the September/October spread is currently quoted at 50 cents to flat, brokers said.
Traders said the latest swap price increase was due to the buying interest of more than one player in the physical market.
On Wednesday, a Dutch trader bid for 20,000 tonnes of fuel oil for lifting September 8-12 but no selling interest emerged against it.
Over the past week, a Singapore trader and a Middle East trader have bought 20,000-tonne cargoes at $103.50 and $102.50 per tonne, respectively, on a free-on-board basis.
Tight supplies in Singapore was clearly reflected in the bunker market where the backwardation is valued at almost $1.00 per tonne per day.
Supplies for lifting over the next few days are priced at up to $5.00 per tonne above the usual products that are sold for delivery 7-10 days out.
The gas oil market edged up slightly in line with the 14 cents overnight rise in September Brent crude values to $19.00 per barrel.
September was last quoted up five cents at $23.40/$23.55 per barrel in quiet trade.
Naphtha also rose in tandem with the crude market with September last quoted at $21.40/$21.60, up from Thursday's $21.30/$21.40, brokers said.
September traded on Wednesday at $21.40 and $21.55, they said.
